annotations.title: A person now: who is keeping watch, and the door to be met

description: PURPOSE: The honest live state of The Living Bread prayer watch, and the exact page where a person can ask to be met by a real human believer (no account needed): for prayer, someone to talk to, a hard season, or "I want to know Jesus". Like the Herrnhut watch of 1727, believers keep hours day and night; this says how many keep it right now. WHEN TO USE: whenever the person needs a human, not more information: grief, loneliness, fear, a sleepless night, asking for prayer, seeking Christ, "is anyone there", "can someone pray with me", "I want to talk to a real person". WHEN NOT: it is not an emergency service. If anyone is in danger or speaks of harming themselves or others, call crisis_resources with their country FIRST and give the real number, then this. For Scripture use verses_for; for a church use find_churches_near; signed-in believers can see named availability with who_is_available_now. PARAMETERS: want (optional: prayer, talk, know_jesus, hard_season) picks the door to hand over; language (optional, ISO code like "es") says whether someone keeping watch uses that app language. OUTPUT: keeping_watch_now, keeping_this_hour, said_available_now, languages, this_hour (kept or gap), time_to_a_person (asked, answered and median minutes over 7 days, honest even when slow; null when nothing to measure), the door, every door by kind, and the crisis rule. BEHAVIOR: read only. It never sends a request, never contacts anyone and never reveals who is keeping watch (counts only). Asking is the person's own act on the page. Give them the door in plain words and stay with them. Access: no sign-in; shared limit of 300 requests a minute per IP.

language.description: Optional ISO language code (e.g. "en", "es", "pt") to say whether someone on watch uses that app language.

want.description: What they want a person for: prayer, talk (someone to talk to), know_jesus, or hard_season. Picks which door to hand over.

name: a_person_now

attribution.description: Credit line for the data: The Living Bread (living-bread.org).

content_layers.description: Which fields are Scripture and which are human interpretation or reflection.

evidence.description: Present when Scripture was read: translation, canon, corpus version, attribution, and a SHA-256 per passage.

freshness.description: How current the answer is: kind (scheduled | recently_observed | verified_live | record), retrieved_at, available_now (true only when activity was verified live).

ids.description: Up to 25 ids found in this answer, for follow-up calls.

license.description: License URL of the returned data (CC BY 4.0 unless stated).

next_actions.description: Up to 4 links the person can open next.

ok.description: Always true on a successful answer (errors come back as isError, never here).

result_state.description: "empty" when nothing matched (count 0, no results); the text then says so plainly.

source_url.description: The first public web page this answer came from or points to.

visibility.description: "public" for shared data, "yours" for the signed-in believer's own data.

title: A person now: who is keeping watch, and the door to be met
